papers.title: The minimal width of universal $p$-adic ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: We determine the minimal width of $p$-adic neural networks with the universal approximation property for continuous $\mathbb Q_p$-valued functions on compact open subsets with respect to the $L_q$ norms and the $C_1$ norm, where the activation function is a natural $p$-adic analogue of the ReLU function.

papers.title: PCF All The Way Down
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.

papers.title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

papers.title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.

papers.title: Prime order torsion on elliptic curves over number fields. Part I: Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotics of the set $S(d)$ of possible prime orders of $K$-rational points on elliptic curves over number fields $K$ of degree $d$ as $d$ tends to infinity. Assuming some conjectures on the sparsity of newforms of weight $2$ and prime level with unexpectedly high analytic rank, we show that $\max S(d) \le 3d + 1$ for sufficiently large even $d$ and $\max S(d) = o(d)$ for odd $d$. This gives a significant (but conjectural) improvement on the currently best known upper bound $\max S(d) \le (3^{d/2} + 1)^2$ due to Oesterl\'e.

papers.title: On the de Rham flip-flopping in dual towers
papers.abstract: We prove a version of de Rham and Hyodo-Kato flip-flopping for dual towers of rigid analytic spaces including those coming from dual basic local Shimura varieties. The main tool are comparison theorems expressing the two cohomologies as pro-\'etale cohomology of corresponding relative period sheaves that, by definition, satisfy pro-\'etale descent. As an application, we show that de Rham and Hyodo-Kato cohomologies of finite level coverings of the Drinfeld space of any dimension $d$ over $K$ are admissible as representations of $\mathbb{GL}_{d+1}(K)$.

papers.title: The Pila-Zannier strategy for Drinfeld modules and Drinfeld modular curves
papers.abstract: We extend the Pila-Zannier strategy to Drinfeld modules: we prove analogues of the Manin-Mumford theorem for a product of two Drinfeld modules of equal rank, and of the Andr\'e-Oort theorem for a product of two Drinfeld modular curves. In characteristic zero, several steps of this strategy rest on $o$-minimality, which has no counterpart over a function field; we replace the counting step by the rigid analytic Pila-Wilkie theorem of Binyamini-Kato, and this appears to be its first arithmetic application. The functional transcendence input, namely an analogue of the Ax-Lindemann theorem in both settings, is established here by an independent point counting argument.

papers.title: Cubic arithmetic-geometric mean and isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves
papers.abstract: We construct degree-three isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic different from three, which correspond to a step of the cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. As an application, we describe the Serre-Tate canonical lift of an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic three by the 3-adic cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. We also discuss the relations of the Hesse curves with complex and finite hypergeometric functions.

papers.title: An Asymptotic for E. P. Stein Numbers
papers.abstract: Epstein's put-or-take-a-square game is an impartial combinatorial game in which a player may, in each turn, add or subtract the largest square not exceeding the current integer. We study E. P. Stein numbers, the positions from which both legal moves lead directly to positive squares, and prove the following asymptotic formula for the counting function $S_2(X)$ of these positions: \[ S_2(X)=\frac{1}{\pi^2}X^{1/4}\log X+O(X^{1/4}). \]

papers.title: Exact $3$-Adic Periods of Symmetric Dellac Numbers and Their Polynomial Extensions
papers.abstract: The odd and even symmetric Dellac numbers are the specializations $a_n=f_n(0)$ and $e_n=f_n(1)$ of the Randrianarivony--Zeng family $f_n(s)=2^{-n}D_n(s)$. Using a finite Stieltjes-fraction truncation, we establish the sharp congruence $v_3(a_n)=1$ for $n\ge2$ and obtain explicit congruences modulo $81$ for both sequences. We also establish universal eventual periodicity modulo arbitrary positive integers. For every integer $s\ge0$ and $k\ge1$, we give and analyse formulas for the \emph{least} eventual period of $f_n(s)$ modulo $3^k$ and its \emph{least starting index}. The period is governed by five linear factors in $s$; the onset follows a nine-class formula modulo $9$. In particular, for $k\ge3$ the even symmetric Dellac period is three times the odd period and begins one index earlier. The proofs combine a finite Stieltjes-fraction certificate, a graded $3$-adic pole expansion, and an explicit finite top-degree certificate over $\F_3$. Finite integer-arithmetic checks supplement the proofs. We also record the connection with the type-$B$ homogenized Linial arrangement.

papers.title: Proof of two conjectures on the log-concavity of partition ranks and cranks
papers.abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang proved that the crank sequence $(M(m,n))_{|m|\le n-1}$ is unimodal for every $n\ge44$. Bringmann, Man, and Rolen subsequently established the unimodality of the rank sequence $(N(m,n))_{|m|\le n-2}$ for every $n\ge39$. Ji and Zang also conjectured that $(M(m,n))_{|m|\le n-71}$ is log-concave for every $n\ge72$, and that $(N(m,n))_{|m|\le n-72}$ is log-concave for every $n\ge73$. In this paper, we prove both conjectures.

papers.title: Partitions with designated summands: $k$-tuples and their congruences
papers.abstract: Let $A_k(n)$ and $B_k(n)$ be the numbers of ordered $k$-tuples of partitions with designated summands, respectively with designated summands and all parts odd, of total size $n$. Using an exact description of the generating function of designated partitions after a $3$-dissection, we classify for every $e$ the values of $k$ for which $A_k(3n+2)$ is divisible by $3^e$: this happens exactly when $k\equiv0$ or $-5\pmod{3^e}$ if $e\le4$, and when $3^e\mid k$ if $e\ge5$. We obtain the corresponding exact $3$-adic and several $2$-adic results for $B_k$ and for $A_k$ along the progressions $4n+3$, a recursion for the classes $3^b(3n+s)$, and for $k=2$ the congruences $A_2(12n+10)\equiv 27f_1^4f_6^3/f_2\pmod{81}$ in generating-function form. We relate the numbers $A_k(n)$ modulo $3$ and $9$ to overpartitions, sums of squares and triangular numbers, give group-action proofs of some of the congruences, and close with several conjectures supported by computation.

papers.title: Multiple $q$-zeta values as polynomials in partition multiplicities
papers.abstract: Writing multiple $q$-zeta values as sums over partitions, a conjecture of Bachmann, proved by Hirose, Maesaka and Watanabe by means of a recursion, says that polynomials in the parts and multiplicities can be replaced by polynomials in the multiplicities alone. We make this replacement explicit, derive from it bounds on weight and depth that make Bachmann's conjecture effective, and provide a closed formula for the Drop1 operator of Hirose, Maesaka, Seki and Watanabe.

papers.title: Time-Averages along Partial Orbits for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate the convergence of time-averages of continuous functions along partial orbits for continuous dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Unlike the classical focus of ergodic theory on convergence almost everywhere, our study emphasizes convergence at every point, motivated by problems in number theory. To this end, we consider a sequence having a uniform behavior property in the natural numbers. We also define and study two structural properties of dynamical systems along such partial orbits: minimal mean Lyapunov stability and minimal mean attractability. Our main result shows that if a continuous dynamical system is both minimally mean Lyapunov stable and minimally mean attractable along a given uniformly behaved sequence, and is minimally uniquely ergodic, then the time-average of any continuous function along the corresponding partial orbit converges to the space average at every point.

papers.title: Distribution of mixed character sums and extremal problems for Littlewood polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove distributional results for mixed character sums \begin{equation*}\sum_{n\le x }\chi(n)e(n\theta),\end{equation*} for fixed $\theta\in [0,1]$ and random character $\chi \pmod q$, as well as for a fixed character $\chi$ and randomly sampled $\theta\in [0,1].$ We present various applications of our results. For example, we construct Littlewood polynomials with large Mahler measure and $L_1$ norm, thus establishing new records in the Mahler and Newman problems. We also prove asymptotics for the $L_{2k}$ norms of well-known Turyn polynomials as $k\to\infty$, refuting a conjecture of G\"unther and Schmidt. An important ingredient in our work is a general way of dealing with "log-integrability" problems.

papers.title: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
papers.abstract: Bloch's identity $\int_\gamma\eta(f,g)=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, relating the regulator of a $K_2$-symbol on an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ to the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product of the divisors, is transmitted in the Mahler-measure literature with $\gamma$ generating the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and factor $1$ (e.g. Lalin-Ramamonjisoa, Thm. 6). We observe that, when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has one connected component ($\Delta<0$), this reading is incompatible with the published intersection-product normalization (Brunault, Proposition 19): the anti-invariant subgroup then has index $2$ in the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$. The correct statement -- factor $1$ for the quotient generator, hence factor $\iota(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for the subgroup generator, with $\iota(E)=1\iff\Delta>0$ -- follows from Brunault's formula by an elementary index computation. We document the phenomenon twice: on 11.a3 by proved values (a Siegel-unit anchor from [Zheng, arXiv:2609.26119]; the diamond side by Brunault and Bertin), and on 20.a4 by high-precision computation of both integrals against the $q$-series for $D_E$ (subgroup/quotient ratio $2$ to $13$ digits). We also show that Touafek's Theorem 2 (involving a $\Delta<0$ curve) mixes two independent normalizations (subgroup versus quotient, and a $(2\pi)^{-1}$ prefactor versus the bare diamond value), and we identify the two-part reinterpretation making its printed formulas mutually compatible. In the cases we have checked, no Mahler-measure or $D_E$-identity is affected: the main theorem of Lalin-Ramamonjisoa (conductor $17$, $\Delta>0$) and Bertin's proved exotic relations stand untouched, and Touafek's final $D_E$-relation is not contradicted and is numerically supported, though its printed derivation retains the gap described in the text. A systematic audit is beyond the scope of this note.

papers.title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^e\mu^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of \[ \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg] \] for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$. The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.

papers.title: On the existence of nonadmissible irreducible smooth representations of $p$-adic $\mathrm{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: Let $p>7$ be a prime, let $n>1$, and let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$ not equal to $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For every extension $E$ of the residue field of $F$, we construct an irreducible smooth $E$-representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ which is not admissible. When $E$ is countable, we also construct such representations without a central character and with nonscalar endomorphisms.

papers.title: Diophantine definability from addition and divisibility over rings of $S$-integers
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $K$ containing the archimedean places, and let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ denote the ring of $S$-integers of $K$. We prove that multiplication is positive-existentially definable in $(\mathcal{O}_{K,S},0,1,+,\mid)$ if and only if the unit group $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}^\times$ is infinite. This extends a 1977 theorem of Lipshitz for rings of integers to rings of $S$-integers. One of the key ingredients is a uniform bound for unit equations due to Evertse, Schlickewei and Schmidt, which we use to recover multiplication on the unit group.

papers.title: Second moment of incomplete Eisenstein series revisited
papers.abstract: We revisit Yu's second moment formula for incomplete Eisenstein series and give uniform bounds for secondary terms appearing in this formula. We use these bounds to improve results on distribution of integer points on the light cone corresponding to an indefinite quadratic form, as well as intrinsic Diophantine approximation on ellipsoids, and counting holonomy vectors of saddle connections of Veech surfaces.

papers.title: Collision Parameters in Higher-Dimensional Families of Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq 3$ and consider the generic family of monic normalized polynomials $f_{\mathbf{t}}(z)=z^d+t_1z^{d-2}+t_2z^{d-3}+\cdots+t_{d-2}z+t_{d-1}$, where $\mathbf{t}=(t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1})$. Given pairwise distinct starting points $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$ and a target point $\beta\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$, we show that the set of parameters $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\in\mathbb{A}^{d-1}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}})$ for which $\beta$ belongs to the forward orbit of every $\alpha_i$ under $f_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$ is not Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^{d-1}$.

papers.title: Twisted Diophantine approximation: asymptotic and uniform results
papers.abstract: Fix an $m\times n$ matrix $A$; twisted Diophantine approximation studies how well we can approximate the affine form $A {\bf q}-{\bf b}$ by an integer $m$-vector, depending on the choice of $m$-vector ${\bf b}$. We report on two companion papers in twisted Diophantine approximation, covering two setups: asymptotic and uniform. The asymptotic paper gives an exact Khintchine-type Lebesgue zero--one law, a null--conull criterion for badly approximable shifts, and Hausdorff-measure tests yielding exact power-law dimensions under a critical divergence condition. The uniform paper computes Hausdorff dimensions of sets of uniformly approximable vectors. It also gives Hausdorff zero--full laws, uniform-exponent spectra, and a sharp escape-of-mass bound. In both cases the results are established for arbitrary approximation functions from suitable regularity classes, and the arguments use a homogeneous lattice count involving all successive minima to record clustering in every independent direction.

papers.title: A Rankin-Selberg Integral for $SU_{2,2}$
papers.abstract: We construct a Rankin-Selberg integral for the non-split quasi-split unitary group $SU_{2,2}$ and prove that it is Eulerian. We then compute the local integral at inert places where all data are unramified, and show that it represents the local adjoint $L$-function of $SU_{2,2}$.

papers.title: Maximal Unipotent Monodromy and $p$-adic Eigenvalue Formulas
papers.abstract: We establish p-adic formulas for the eigenvalues of Frobenius in the case of the family of hyperkloosterman sums. The deformation equation in this case has maximal unipotent monodromy, and the interplay of Frobenius and the differential equation plays an important role in establishing p-adic analytic formulas for the eigenvalues.

papers.title: The enhanced polylogarithm conjecture in weight two for imaginary quadratic fields
papers.abstract: Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture predicts that special values of Dedekind zeta functions can be expressed in terms of polylogarithms at algebraic arguments. For imaginary quadratic fields, Zagier and Gangl refined it by lifting both sides to complex values modulo rational multiples of a power of $2\pi i$. In previous work, the author extended their enhanced zeta values from ideal classes to ray classes by means of the Shintani $L$-function of two variables and formulated the enhanced polylogarithm conjecture for ray classes. In this article, we prove this conjecture in weight two. More precisely, we establish a Galois-equivariant equality between the enhanced partial zeta values of ray classes and the enhanced dilogarithms of elements of the rational Bloch groups of the corresponding ray class fields. These elements are constructed explicitly, starting from the Eisenstein class of Doran and Kerr on the square of a CM elliptic curve and contracting it with the graphs of complex multiplication.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: The Minimal excludant of $\ell$-regular partition
papers.abstract: Andrews and Newman \cite{andrewsnewmanI} introduced and studied ``mex,'' function for an integer partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$. The related function $\sigma^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ was subsequently defined, and its generating function and other properties have been studied by several authors. In this article, for a positive integer $\ell \geq 2$, we define the minimal excludant of an $\ell$-regular partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$. We then define $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, the sum of the minimal excludants over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$, and obtain explicit generating functions for $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ in the cases $\ell = 2$ and $\ell = 3$, expressed as eta-quotients. We prove that the sequence $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell$, and we obtain Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ and $\sigma_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. Additionally, we completely determine the parity of $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, showing that it is odd precisely at generalized pentagonal numbers, and we use this characterization to compute the density of $n$ for which $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is odd versus even. Finally, for $\sigma_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, we prove that it is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such $n$ up to $X$ grows at least like $\log \log X$.

papers.title: A Galois-type Springer theorem for hermitian and generalized quadratic forms
papers.abstract: We prove that anisotropy of nonsingular hermitian and skew-hermitian forms over central simple algebras with involution is preserved under scalar extension to every finite Galois extension of odd degree coprime to the index of the algebra. In characteristic two, the same conclusion holds for generalized quadratic forms over algebras with involution of the first kind, with no nonsingularity assumption on their polar forms. The main tool is an isometry-level descent theorem. For a cyclic extension of odd prime degree, every anisotropic nonsingular form over a division algebra with involution, of rank smaller than the extension degree and with Galois-invariant isometry class, descends to an anisotropic form over the base field. Unlike descent results for Witt classes, this theorem descends the form itself. A bounded-rank reduction, based on injectivity of the Witt-group restriction map, derives the cyclic anisotropy theorem from this descent result; a regularization argument removes the nonsingularity assumption on polar forms in characteristic two, and the Feit-Thompson theorem extends the result to arbitrary finite Galois extensions of odd degree.

papers.title: Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound $\Lambda<0.156821$ for the de Bruijn--Newman Constant
papers.abstract: The de Bruijn--Newman constant $\Lambda$ is the transition time beyond which all zeros of the heat-deformed Riemann $\xi$-function are real. We develop a computer-assisted collision-exclusion method and obtain the bound $\Lambda<156821/10^6=0.156821$, in the normalisation of Polymath. The proof combines the published finite-height verification and the starting inequality $\Lambda\leq1/5$ with a compact-interior continuation theorem, five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, certified moving-index recovery, a balanced real-jet transfer and a uniform Euler-product barrier at infinity. The resulting closed time-band exclusion, together with uniform remote reality, forces strictness at the proposed endpoint. The finite certificate uses 664,505 structural Fourier coefficients, 44,182 closed torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles. We isolate a Cauchy--Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, explaining the narrow feasibility margin of the certified endpoint. We state the proof-to-certificate interface and distinguish the present unconditional logical claim from other recent, as yet unrefereed, computational bounds.

papers.title: Hopf-Galois Structures on Extensions Arising from Division Points on Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We provide a general construction of infinite Hopf-Galois extensions from a direct system of finite Hopf-Galois extensions. We then apply this framework to extensions generated by division points on elliptic curves. Specifically, for a number field $K$ and an elliptic curve $E/K$ of rank at least $1$ with $P\in E(K)$ of infinite order, we consider for each integer $n\geq 2$ the extension $L_n=K(Q_n)$, where $Q_n\in E(\overline{K})$ is such that $nQ_n=P$. We show that the finite-level extensions $L_n/K$ need not be Hopf-Galois, and we give sufficient conditions for them to be so. We then prove that the infinite extension $L_\infty=\bigcup_{n\geq 2}L_n$ of $K$ is potentially Hopf-Galois, meaning it becomes Hopf-Galois after a finite extension of the base field.
